purpose: Guide Avatar Builder when Robert wants a character to look more physically real than a movie/cartoon/comic source while still preserving recognizable identity.
core_rule: Do not make a flat cartoon, comic-strip copy, cosplay copy, toy copy, or copied reference model. Build a realistic synthetic-person avatar from an approved base body and use source images as identity, silhouette, hairstyle, clothing, expression, and color references.
realism_targets: real 3D head volume with skull, jaw, cheek, brow, nose, lip, and ear structure
eyes are round movable eyeballs in sockets with eyelids, lashes, brows, iris depth, cornea, and catchlights
mouth opens with lips, teeth, tongue, jaw controls, and speech/lip-sync shape keys
skin shader uses subtle pores, roughness variation, blush/freckle detail, and subsurface scattering where appropriate
hair is built as real hair cards/curves or sculpted clumps with roots, parting, layered strands, flyaways, and variant hairstyles
body starts from the correct adult/non-adult base policy, then is shaped toward references without copying a reference model
clothing is separate wearable garment geometry unless explicitly a magic/morph suit exception
source_priority: Robert-approved movie/episode frames or official stills
multi-angle turnarounds that clarify silhouette and proportions
high-quality fan/concept references only for secondary realism, not as authority over canon/approved frames
comic panels only as design and identity references, not as literal anatomy or final render style
comic_strip_rule: Comic strips can help identify suit markings, color blocks, pose language, and recurring identity cues. They should not drive realistic head anatomy, body anatomy, eye placement, or final skin/hair realism.
must_not_do: do not paste flat eye planes onto the face
do not use photos of actors or voice actors as character likeness unless Robert explicitly asks for that separate person
do not copy a reference model head/body as the active avatar
do not use non-adult body policy on an adult character
do not use adult anatomy references for non-adult characters
do not mark a realistic adaptation as passed without front, side, three-quarter, mouth-open, eye-socket, and body/suit proof renders
